# wri-power-plants

**WRI's Global Power Plant Database, for the infrastructure layers outside the US**

- **Version recorded:** 1.3.0
- **Categories:** `emcomm`, `navigation-maps`
- **Upstream:** <https://datasets.wri.org/dataset/globalpowerplantdatabase>

## What it does

Installs one file, WRI's Global Power Plant Database v1.3.0 as a zipped CSV (about 4.2 MB), under /usr/local/share/hammunition/data/wri-power-plants/. Nothing reads it on its own: `hammunition maps infra import --from-wri` turns the plants in your map regions, outside the US, into a layer for QMapShack, Navit, phones and the browser map, each with its capacity, fuel, owner and commissioning year, credited "WRI Global Power Plant Database v1.3.0 (2021), CC BY 4.0".

## Why you would want it

It is the only worldwide plant list found under an open licence that can be pinned: Canada's, Europe's and the UK's regulators publish theirs in many shapes and licences, and none as one file. For a station whose regions reach past the US border, it is the plant layer.

## Before it will work

Map regions installed (`hammunition install osm-regions`): the import keeps what lies in their boxes. QMapShack, Navit or the browser map to see the layer.

## Install and launch

- **Installed by name only** — it is in no profile.
- **Install:** `hammunition install wri-power-plants --dry-run`, read the plan, then run it without `--dry-run`.
- **Launch:** Its package ships its own commands and application-menu entry; a unit that ships none gets a generated terminal entry (**D-050**). `hammunition status` lists what is installed.
- **The install needs the network to:** the upstream files the plan lists, each checked against a pinned digest (or, for map and reference data, the publisher or a LAN mirror).

## Offline use

*Not yet documented for this application.* Read “Before it will work” above for what it needs; the install-time network line above is the only offline fact generated from the manifest. Internet, a local network and a radio link are three different things, and this page does not claim any of them works until it says so.

## How it installs

- data (CC-BY-4.0, https://datasets.wri.org/dataset/globalpowerplantdatabase): https://wri-dataportal-prod.s3.amazonaws.com/manual/global_power_plant_database_v_1_3.zip (4,178,889 bytes)

## Known problems

Frozen in 2021: plants built since are missing and some retired ones remain. US plants are left out of the layer, by design (`eia-860m` covers the US). CC BY 4.0 asks for the credit the layer carries; keep it if you share the layer.

## Keeping it current

- probe: none
- strategy: reinstall
- Frozen since 2021: WRI no longer updates it. The weekly pin review runs `scripts/gen_wri_pin.py --check`, a HEAD that goes red if the file's ETag or size ever change; regenerating checks the new bytes' MD5 against the ETag before it writes anything.

## Where to get help with the software itself

World Resources Institute's dataset page (https://datasets.wri.org/dataset/globalpowerplantdatabase); the database is no longer maintained, so corrections go to the national sources it was built from. Hammunition only converts the file.
